name: M5Stack Unit Ultrasonic-I2C distance sensor
description: Ultrasonic distance sensor unit: an RCWL-9620 ranging chip driving a 16 mm open probe pair, read over I2C at address 0x57. Range 2-450 cm, ±2 %, 1 mm resolution, about 3 mA. Write 0x01 to start a measurement, wait at least 100 ms, then read 3 bytes: distance = 24-bit value / 1000 mm. The chip runs on 2.8-5.5 V straight from the Grove supply pin; its SDA/SCL are open-drain I2C lines and the chip's reference design has no pull-ups on them, so the host provides them. Sold as: M5Stack Unit Ultrasonic-I2C (SKU U098-B1, RCWL-9620), 4-pin HY2.0-4P Grove connector GND, 5V, SDA, SCL, supplied with a 20 cm Grove cable.
eli5: Sends out a chirp too high to hear and times the echo, so it can tell how far away a wall or your hand is.

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: Supply (pin 2, red wire; labelled 5V on M5Stack's PORT.A). Goes straight to the RCWL-9620, which runs on 2.8-5.5 V. With an ESP32 / Pico / Raspberry Pi feed it 3.3 V so the chip and the I2C pull-ups share the board's 3.3 V logic level.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (pin 3, yellow wire), open-drain; needs a pull-up to the supply (M5Stack controllers have one; add 4.7 kΩ otherwise)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (pin 4, white wire), open-drain; needs a pull-up to the supply (M5Stack controllers have one; add 4.7 kΩ otherwise)

supplierQuery: M5Stack Unit Ultrasonic I2C RCWL-9620 U098-B1
buildNotes: Start a measurement by writing the single byte 0x01 to address 0x57, wait at least 100 ms (M5Stack's library waits 120 ms), then read 3 bytes. Distance in mm = ((b0 << 16) | (b1 << 8) | b2) / 1000.
Do not read faster than the 50 ms measurement cycle; one reading every 150 ms or slower is reliable. M5Stack notes replies can be slower beyond 3.5 m.
The chip's reference circuit has no I2C pull-ups: Sparkbench adds 4.7 kΩ from SDA and SCL to the supply. Run the unit from 3.3 V on 3.3 V boards so nothing on the bus is pulled above 3.3 V.
Readings under about 2 cm (the blind zone) are random; soft or angled surfaces (cloth, a slanted wall) may give no echo or a long reading. Readings above 4500 mm mean out of range.
Point the two probes squarely at the target; the beam is about 60° wide, so nearby edges and table tops can echo first.

driver.code:
# M5Stack Unit Ultrasonic-I2C (RCWL-9620 ultrasonic ranging chip), MicroPython driver.
# RCWL-9620 datasheet, I2C mode: address 0x57. Write command 0x01 to start a measurement,
# wait at least 100 ms (the chip's longest measurement time), then read 3 bytes
# BYTE_H, BYTE_M, BYTE_L: distance = ((BYTE_H << 16) + (BYTE_M << 8) + BYTE_L) / 1000 mm.
import time

MAX_MM = 4500  # M5Stack's specified range is 20-4500 mm


class RCWL9620:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x57):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def distance_mm(self):
        """Start one measurement and return the distance in millimetres (capped at 4500)."""
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x01')
        time.sleep_ms(120)  # datasheet: wait 100 ms or more before reading
        d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 3)
        mm = ((d[0] << 16) | (d[1] << 8) | d[2]) / 1000
        return MAX_MM if mm > MAX_MM else mm

    def distance_cm(self):
        return self.distance_mm() / 10

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from rcwl9620 import RCWL9620

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sonic = RCWL9620(i2c)
while True:
    print('D=%.1fmm' % sonic.distance_mm())
    time.sleep_ms(200)
